trust_decision.summary: pruneBackups treats the `path` field of each backup's _manifest.json (reloaded unfiltered by listBackups) as a trusted filesystem target and recursively deletes it; the deletion target must instead be derived from a validated backupId confined to that environment's .backups directory, because the manifest is attacker-writable state, not configuration the manager controls.

landing_point.why: The summary says a poisoned backup manifest drives arbitrary recursive deletion during backup pruning; the only recursive delete of a manifest-supplied path in the tree is this rmSync(entry.path, {recursive:true, force:true}).

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `network-ai env backup prune` (bin/cli.ts:471), `env backup create` (bin/cli.ts:419), `env backup restore` (bin/cli.ts:457), `env promote` (bin/cli.ts:399); library EnvironmentManager.pruneBackups/backup/restore exported at index.ts:1563; TransportAgent.execute (lib/transport-agent.ts:351,363,396)
fix_sites.module_kind: library module — environment data plane (per-env data directories, backup/restore/prune)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: n/a — there is no O2 site and no O8 route: every public surface funnels into the single pruneBackups loop, so there is nothing a solver could argue out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every legitimate manifest stores an absolute `path` (backup() writes the resolved backupPath), and prune must actually delete old backups — test-env-manager.ts:487-497 asserts deleted > 0 and that at most `keep` remain, while test-env-manager.ts:527 reads firstBackup.path as a real directory. A fix that rejects absolute paths, requires a relative path, or filters entries by their manifest path silently disables pruning, so backups grow without bound and the round-trip test fails; the fix must recompute the target from backupId rather than reject by path.

O6_input_shapes: manifest `path` = absolute path outside the environment (`/`, `/etc`), the summary's example
manifest `path` = sibling of the backups dir sharing its name prefix (`<env>/.backups-evil`) or the backups dir itself
manifest `backupId` containing `/`, `.` or `..` when the target is recomputed from backupId
canonical generated IDs (`2026-06-18T12-00-00-000Z_ab12cd34`) and stale absolute `path` values from a relocated data dir must still prune
